If instead you build a new gate component and leave `AccountPanel` intact, `/join` is unaffected. Worth deciding explicitly.

## 6. Existing tests & the exact locator strings they depend on

**Unit/component (bun + testing-library):**
- `components/menu/ProfileSelect.test.tsx` — first-run asserts "Create Your Profile", label "Profile name", **buttons "Sign in" + "Create account"** (`:31-32`), no "Cancel"; `back-to-account` testid present with door / absent without (`:35-48,50-60`); list plays `profile-<id>`, `new-profile`, rename/delete. - `components/menu/AccountProfileSelect.test.tsx` — `online-profile-<id>`, "Signed in as Keeper", `new-online-profile`, **`play-locally` testid ("the Play locally door notifies the parent", `:83-91`)**, sign-out. Deleting the door breaks this test.
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.test.tsx` — drives `cloudEnabled` true/false: "Upload to cloud", "☁ Synced", `cloud-world-<id>`, "Cloud Saves", `listCalls===0` when logged out.
- `components/menu/OnlineWorldSelect.test.tsx`, `CreateWorldForm.test.tsx`, `lib/game/profiles.test.ts` — adjacent, not gating the welcome flow.

**e2e (Playwright) — locator strings in order per spec:**

- `e2e/menu.e2e.ts` (logged out, empty storage): every test opens with `createProfile()` helper (`:11-14`) = `getByLabel("Profile name").fill` → `getByRole("button",{name:"Create"})`. Then `new-world`, `getByLabel("World name")`, `getByLabel("World seed")`, `getByRole("button",{name:"Create World"})`, `back-to-profiles`, `new-profile`. **No account panel.** A welcome chooser inserted before the first-run form breaks the very first `getByLabel("Profile name")` unless the helper first clicks the new "Play locally" choice.

Depends on both the "Sign in" open-form entry point and the `play-locally` door.

# Where the "DATABASE_URL is not set" error lives, and every graceful-degradation lever

## 1. The throw site — lazy, on first `db()` call

`/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/db/index.ts:21-24`

```ts
export function db(): Db {
  if (instance) return instance;
  const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL;
  if (!url) throw new Error("DATABASE_URL is not set — see .env.example");
```

- **Lazy, NOT at module load.** Importing `@/db` is safe (the header comment at `db/index.ts:5-10` says so explicitly — the client bundle types against the schema, only route handlers/game server actually connect). The throw only fires the first time `db()` is *called* at runtime, then the result is memoized in `instance` (`db/index.ts:19`).
- `auth()` (`lib/auth/server.ts:45-47`) is also lazy and calls `db()` inside `createAuth(db())`, so the throw propagates through the auth layer too.

## 2. What triggers `db()` during local play

Every `db()` call site is inside an `app/api/**` route handler or `lib/auth/server.ts` (confirmed by grep — 17 call sites, all under `app/api/` plus the one in `lib/auth/server.ts:46`). Nothing calls `db()` at import/module scope. So the error can only fire in response to an HTTP request to `/api/*`.

**The offline-first gate** — `lib/auth/client.ts:36-44`: the `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage flag (`ONLINE_USED_KEY`). `onlineUsed()` reads it; `markOnlineUsed()` sets it. It is set in exactly **two** places:
- `components/menu/AccountPanel.tsx:57` — inside `submit()`, when the user actually submits the sign-in / register form.
- `app/join/[token]/page.tsx:35` — on mount of the invite landing page (`/join/[token]`).

Both are explicit online actions. Nothing sets it on a normal page load.

**Mount-time probes that are gated by `onlineUsed()`:**
- `GameShell.tsx:117-123` `refreshOnlineUser()` → guarded by `if (onlineUsed())` → `currentUser()` (`lib/auth/client.ts:47`) → `authClient().getSession()` → **`GET /api/auth/get-session`** → better-auth handler → `auth()` → `createAuth(db())` → `db()`. Invoked at mount via `GameShell.tsx:256`.
- `AccountPanel.tsx:26-30` — same guard `if (onlineUsed()) void currentUser()`.

**Other `/api/*` callers on load:** none unconditional. The world/profile list fetches (`listOnlineWorlds` at `OnlineWorldSelect.tsx:65`, `listOnlineProfiles` at `AccountProfileSelect.tsx:41-42`) only run when those components are mounted, and they only mount once `onlineUser !== null` (account mode, `GameShell.tsx:392-402`) — which itself requires a successful session probe. `cloudSaves` fetches only fire when opening a cloud-linked world.

**Conclusion:**
- **Truly fresh browser:** `onlineUsed()` is false → no session probe → no `/api/*` request → **the error never fires.** Offline-first works exactly as designed. The game is fully playable.
- **Browser that once went online (the developer's own):** the flag persists in localStorage. On every page load `GameShell.tsx:256` → `refreshOnlineUser()` → `currentUser()` → `GET /api/auth/get-session` → `db()` throws. **This is the repro.** It is stale localStorage from prior online use, not fresh local play.

## 3. Where the error surfaces

- **Server/terminal:** `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts:11` `mount()` calls `auth()` synchronously, which calls `db()` which throws. The GET handler throws → Next.js returns **HTTP 500 with a full stack trace printed in the `bun run dev` terminal** on every load (for the online-flagged browser). Same would happen for any `/api/worlds`, `/api/profiles`, etc.
- **Client:** `currentUser()` (`lib/auth/client.ts:47-52`) has **no try/catch**. It relies on better-auth's client `getSession()` returning `{ data, error }` rather than throwing (better-auth uses better-fetch, which by default does not throw on HTTP errors; the client is constructed with only `baseURL` at `lib/auth/client.ts:19-22`, no `throw: true`). On a 500 → `data` is null → `if (!data?.user) return null` → `currentUser()` resolves to **null**.
- **Net effect on UI:** `GameShell` sets `onlineUser = null` → stays in local `ProfileSelect` mode (`GameShell.tsx:404-413`). `AccountPanel` shows the "Offline" state (`AccountPanel.tsx:121-132`). So the player is **silently treated as logged-out — no error UI** — while the terminal spews a 500 stack on every load. (Minor caveat: if better-auth's `getSession` ever rejected instead of returning `{error}`, the un-`.catch`ed `void currentUser().then(...)` at `GameShell.tsx:119` / `AccountPanel.tsx:29` would become an unhandled rejection. In practice it returns `{error}`, so this stays graceful.)
- The online *fetch* helpers (`onlineClient.ts`, `profilesClient.ts`) are all wrapped in try/catch returning null/false (see `onlineClient.ts:13-118`), so any that do fire degrade cleanly to "offline" states.

## 4. The `pglite://memory` escape hatch

`db/index.ts:25-40`: if `DATABASE_URL` starts with `pglite:`, it lazy-`require`s `@electric-sql/pglite` + `drizzle-orm/pglite` + `./ddl`, spins up an in-process `new PGlite()`, applies `SCHEMA_DDL` (`db/ddl.ts`) async, and returns a drizzle-pglite instance. Data lives exactly as long as the process (comment `db/index.ts:12-14`).

- **Deps present?** Yes. `@electric-sql/pglite` `^0.5.4` is in `package.json:30` (devDependencies) and `drizzle-orm` provides the `/pglite` adapter. `next.config.mjs` already has `serverExternalPackages: ["@electric-sql/pglite"]` so the WASM resolves at runtime. It is a **devDependency**, so a production install (`--production`) would not have it — fine for dev, but relevant if you ever wanted this branch in prod.
- **Would `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory bun run dev` give a fully-working ephemeral online stack today?** **Yes, for the web/auth side.** `db()` uses pglite. And **better-auth does NOT hard-require `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` in dev**: `node_modules/better-auth/dist/context/create-context.mjs:49` falls back to `DEFAULT_SECRET = "better-auth-secret-12345678901234567890"`, and line 41 only throws `if (isDefaultSecret && isProduction)`. `isProduction` = `NODE_ENV === "production"` (`@better-auth/core/dist/env/env-impl.mjs:32`). `next dev` sets `NODE_ENV=development`, so the default secret is accepted with only low-entropy warnings. So sign-up / sign-in / sessions / cloud saves all work ephemerally. (`BETTER_AUTH_URL` is also optional — it defaults from the request; the auth client uses `window.location.origin` at `lib/auth/client.ts:20`.) Multiplayer *realtime* still needs the separate Bun game server + `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` + `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`, but accounts/worlds/cloud-single-player would function.
- **Important asymmetry:** Playwright (`playwright.config.ts:32-42`) uses `bun run build && bun run start` (production, `NODE_ENV=production`), which is exactly why it *must* set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: "e2e-secret-…"` — the default secret would throw there. In dev you don't need it.
- Documented in `docs/online.md:155-160` ("No Docker at all") and `.env.example` (which documents the full Postgres setup, not the pglite shortcut).

## 5. better-auth server config (`lib/auth/server.ts`)

- `auth()` is **lazy** (`lib/auth/server.ts:42-47`, memoized `instance`). Importing the module needs no env (comment `lib/auth/server.ts:44`).
- `createAuth` reads `process.env.BETTER_AUTH_URL` (`server.ts:18`) and `process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (`server.ts:19`), but only passes them into `betterAuth({...})`; **betterAuth's context (and thus secret validation) initializes lazily on the first API call**, not at `auth()` construction.
- Hard-require at call time: **only the DB** (via `createAuth(db())` → `db()` throws first if `DATABASE_URL` is missing — this is what fires today). `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is *soft* in dev (default-secret fallback), *hard* in production (throws `BetterAuthError`). `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is optional (request-derived).

## 6. Existing "is online configured?" signals

**There is none for the DB/web side.** Grep for `NEXT_PUBLIC` finds only:
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS` (`lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:118`) — latency sim.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` (`app/api/worlds/[id]/ticket/route.ts:24`, `.env.example:15`) — the realtime game-server URL, returned in the ticket response and used to decide realtime availability (`onlineClient.ts:113` returns null if unset). This gates *multiplayer*, not accounts/DB.

There's no web-app health endpoint (only the *game server* has `/health`, `playwright.config.ts:47`). The client's only "online available?" heuristic today is `onlineUser !== null` (i.e., "did the session probe succeed?"), used for `cloudEnabled` at `GameShell.tsx:366`. So option (c) would require a *new* `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` flag — none exists to reuse.

## 7. How dev runs / env loading

- `package.json:6` — `"dev": "next dev"`. Plain, no dotenv wrapper, no inline env.
- **Env loading is Next.js built-in.** `next dev` auto-loads `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.development`, `.env.development.local` from the project root if present. **None exist today** — only `.env.example` (`ls` + `git ls-files` confirm; `.env.example` is not auto-loaded). `.gitignore` doesn't even list `.env*` (it lists `.next`, `node_modules`, etc.), so there's no committed-secret hygiene beyond convention.
- `bun run dev` passes the shell environment through, so `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory bun run dev` (or exporting vars / creating a `.env.local`) all work. `bunfig.toml` only configures the test preload, nothing dev-related.
- So today, bare `bun run dev` → `DATABASE_URL` undefined → the first `/api/*` hit throws.

---

## Decision inputs for (a) / (b) / (c)

**(a) API routes catch missing-DB and return a clean "online not configured" response.** Smallest blast radius. The natural seam is `sessionUser()` in `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/online/http.ts:13-18` (it already wraps `auth()`), plus the raw `db()` calls in each route and the better-auth mount `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts:13-19`. A `try/catch` mapping the missing-DB error to e.g. 503 `{error:"online-not-configured"}` would turn the terminal 500-stack into a clean response; the client already treats non-OK as logged-out/offline (`currentUser` → null, `onlineClient`/`profilesClient` → null/false), so **no client changes are strictly required** to stop the crash — but the auth route is the one that actually fires on load and would need the same treatment. Note there is no single choke point: 17 `db()` sites + the auth mount.

**(b) `db()` falls back to `pglite://memory` in dev.** One-line-ish change at `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/db/index.ts:23-24` (e.g. default `url` to `pglite://memory` when unset and `NODE_ENV !== "production"`). Gives a *fully working* ephemeral online stack in dev with zero env (secret default already works in dev, per §4/§5). Caveats: `@electric-sql/pglite` is a **devDependency** (fine for dev, would need care to never trigger in prod), data is ephemeral per restart, and this silently changes today's "offline-first, no accounts" behavior into "accounts work but reset on restart" — which may surprise. Must keep the hard throw for `NODE_ENV=production`.

**(c) `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` flag hides online UI when no DB.** No such flag exists (§6) — you'd add one (e.g. `NEXT_PUBLIC_ONLINE_ENABLED`) and gate `AccountPanel` (sign-in/register buttons), the `onlineUsed()` probes in `GameShell.tsx:118` / `AccountPanel.tsx:29`, and the invite page. Purely cosmetic/preventive; doesn't fix an already-flagged browser unless the flag also short-circuits `currentUser()`. Cleanest "the developer never sees the 500" story, but most touch points.

**Key nuance for whichever you pick:** the bug only reproduces on a browser whose `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage flag is already set from prior online use (§2). A fresh browser is already fine today. So (b) or (a) address the *server crash*; (c) plus a check on `onlineUsed()` addresses the *stale-flag probe*. Combining (a) — so the auth route degrades cleanly — with a dev default in (b) would both silence the terminal and make local online dev zero-config.

- **Lazy, NOT at module load.** Importing `@/db` is safe (the header comment at `db/index.ts:5-10` says so explicitly — the client bundle types against the schema, only route handlers/game server actually connect). The throw only fires the first time `db()` is *called* at runtime, then the result is memoized in `instance` (`db/index.ts:19`).
- `auth()` (`lib/auth/server.ts:45-47`) is also lazy and calls `db()` inside `createAuth(db())`, so the throw propagates through the auth layer too.

## 2. What triggers `db()` during local play

Every `db()` call site is inside an `app/api/**` route handler or `lib/auth/server.ts` (confirmed by grep — 17 call sites, all under `app/api/` plus the one in `lib/auth/server.ts:46`). Nothing calls `db()` at import/module scope. So the error can only fire in response to an HTTP request to `/api/*`.

**The offline-first gate** — `lib/auth/client.ts:36-44`: the `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage flag (`ONLINE_USED_KEY`). `onlineUsed()` reads it; `markOnlineUsed()` sets it. It is set in exactly **two** places:
- `components/menu/AccountPanel.tsx:57` — inside `submit()`, when the user actually submits the sign-in / register form.
- `app/join/[token]/page.tsx:35` — on mount of the invite landing page (`/join/[token]`).

Both are explicit online actions. Nothing sets it on a normal page load.

**Mount-time probes that are gated by `onlineUsed()`:**
- `GameShell.tsx:117-123` `refreshOnlineUser()` → guarded by `if (onlineUsed())` → `currentUser()` (`lib/auth/client.ts:47`) → `authClient().getSession()` → **`GET /api/auth/get-session`** → better-auth handler → `auth()` → `createAuth(db())` → `db()`. Invoked at mount via `GameShell.tsx:256`.
- `AccountPanel.tsx:26-30` — same guard `if (onlineUsed()) void currentUser()`.

**Other `/api/*` callers on load:** none unconditional. The world/profile list fetches (`listOnlineWorlds` at `OnlineWorldSelect.tsx:65`, `listOnlineProfiles` at `AccountProfileSelect.tsx:41-42`) only run when those components are mounted, and they only mount once `onlineUser !== null` (account mode, `GameShell.tsx:392-402`) — which itself requires a successful session probe. `cloudSaves` fetches only fire when opening a cloud-linked world.

**Conclusion:**
- **Truly fresh browser:** `onlineUsed()` is false → no session probe → no `/api/*` request → **the error never fires.** Offline-first works exactly as designed. The game is fully playable.
- **Browser that once went online (the developer's own):** the flag persists in localStorage. On every page load `GameShell.tsx:256` → `refreshOnlineUser()` → `currentUser()` → `GET /api/auth/get-session` → `db()` throws. **This is the repro.** It is stale localStorage from prior online use, not fresh local play.

## 3. Where the error surfaces

- **Server/terminal:** `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts:11` `mount()` calls `auth()` synchronously, which calls `db()` which throws. The GET handler throws → Next.js returns **HTTP 500 with a full stack trace printed in the `bun run dev` terminal** on every load (for the online-flagged browser). Same would happen for any `/api/worlds`, `/api/profiles`, etc.
- **Client:** `currentUser()` (`lib/auth/client.ts:47-52`) has **no try/catch**. It relies on better-auth's client `getSession()` returning `{ data, error }` rather than throwing (better-auth uses better-fetch, which by default does not throw on HTTP errors; the client is constructed with only `baseURL` at `lib/auth/client.ts:19-22`, no `throw: true`). On a 500 → `data` is null → `if (!data?.user) return null` → `currentUser()` resolves to **null**.
- **Net effect on UI:** `GameShell` sets `onlineUser = null` → stays in local `ProfileSelect` mode (`GameShell.tsx:404-413`). `AccountPanel` shows the "Offline" state (`AccountPanel.tsx:121-132`). So the player is **silently treated as logged-out — no error UI** — while the terminal spews a 500 stack on every load. (Minor caveat: if better-auth's `getSession` ever rejected instead of returning `{error}`, the un-`.catch`ed `void currentUser().then(...)` at `GameShell.tsx:119` / `AccountPanel.tsx:29` would become an unhandled rejection. In practice it returns `{error}`, so this stays graceful.)
- The online *fetch* helpers (`onlineClient.ts`, `profilesClient.ts`) are all wrapped in try/catch returning null/false (see `onlineClient.ts:13-118`), so any that do fire degrade cleanly to "offline" states.

## 4. The `pglite://memory` escape hatch

`db/index.ts:25-40`: if `DATABASE_URL` starts with `pglite:`, it lazy-`require`s `@electric-sql/pglite` + `drizzle-orm/pglite` + `./ddl`, spins up an in-process `new PGlite()`, applies `SCHEMA_DDL` (`db/ddl.ts`) async, and returns a drizzle-pglite instance. Data lives exactly as long as the process (comment `db/index.ts:12-14`).

- **Deps present?** Yes. `@electric-sql/pglite` `^0.5.4` is in `package.json:30` (devDependencies) and `drizzle-orm` provides the `/pglite` adapter. `next.config.mjs` already has `serverExternalPackages: ["@electric-sql/pglite"]` so the WASM resolves at runtime. It is a **devDependency**, so a production install (`--production`) would not have it — fine for dev, but relevant if you ever wanted this branch in prod.
- **Would `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory bun run dev` give a fully-working ephemeral online stack today?** **Yes, for the web/auth side.** `db()` uses pglite. And **better-auth does NOT hard-require `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` in dev**: `node_modules/better-auth/dist/context/create-context.mjs:49` falls back to `DEFAULT_SECRET = "better-auth-secret-12345678901234567890"`, and line 41 only throws `if (isDefaultSecret && isProduction)`. `isProduction` = `NODE_ENV === "production"` (`@better-auth/core/dist/env/env-impl.mjs:32`). `next dev` sets `NODE_ENV=development`, so the default secret is accepted with only low-entropy warnings. So sign-up / sign-in / sessions / cloud saves all work ephemerally. (`BETTER_AUTH_URL` is also optional — it defaults from the request; the auth client uses `window.location.origin` at `lib/auth/client.ts:20`.) Multiplayer *realtime* still needs the separate Bun game server + `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` + `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`, but accounts/worlds/cloud-single-player would function.
- **Important asymmetry:** Playwright (`playwright.config.ts:32-42`) uses `bun run build && bun run start` (production, `NODE_ENV=production`), which is exactly why it *must* set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: "e2e-secret-…"` — the default secret would throw there. In dev you don't need it.
- Documented in `docs/online.md:155-160` ("No Docker at all") and `.env.example` (which documents the full Postgres setup, not the pglite shortcut).

## 5. better-auth server config (`lib/auth/server.ts`)

- `auth()` is **lazy** (`lib/auth/server.ts:42-47`, memoized `instance`). Importing the module needs no env (comment `lib/auth/server.ts:44`).
- `createAuth` reads `process.env.BETTER_AUTH_URL` (`server.ts:18`) and `process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (`server.ts:19`), but only passes them into `betterAuth({...})`; **betterAuth's context (and thus secret validation) initializes lazily on the first API call**, not at `auth()` construction.
- Hard-require at call time: **only the DB** (via `createAuth(db())` → `db()` throws first if `DATABASE_URL` is missing — this is what fires today). `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is *soft* in dev (default-secret fallback), *hard* in production (throws `BetterAuthError`). `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is optional (request-derived).

## 6. Existing "is online configured?" signals

**There is none for the DB/web side.** Grep for `NEXT_PUBLIC` finds only:
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS` (`lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:118`) — latency sim.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` (`app/api/worlds/[id]/ticket/route.ts:24`, `.env.example:15`) — the realtime game-server URL, returned in the ticket response and used to decide realtime availability (`onlineClient.ts:113` returns null if unset). This gates *multiplayer*, not accounts/DB.

There's no web-app health endpoint (only the *game server* has `/health`, `playwright.config.ts:47`). The client's only "online available?" heuristic today is `onlineUser !== null` (i.e., "did the session probe succeed?"), used for `cloudEnabled` at `GameShell.tsx:366`. So option (c) would require a *new* `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` flag — none exists to reuse.

## 7. How dev runs / env loading

- `package.json:6` — `"dev": "next dev"`. Plain, no dotenv wrapper, no inline env.
- **Env loading is Next.js built-in.** `next dev` auto-loads `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.development`, `.env.development.local` from the project root if present. **None exist today** — only `.env.example` (`ls` + `git ls-files` confirm; `.env.example` is not auto-loaded). `.gitignore` doesn't even list `.env*` (it lists `.next`, `node_modules`, etc.), so there's no committed-secret hygiene beyond convention.
- `bun run dev` passes the shell environment through, so `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory bun run dev` (or exporting vars / creating a `.env.local`) all work. `bunfig.toml` only configures the test preload, nothing dev-related.
- So today, bare `bun run dev` → `DATABASE_URL` undefined → the first `/api/*` hit throws.

---

## Decision inputs for (a) / (b) / (c)

**(a) API routes catch missing-DB and return a clean "online not configured" response.** Smallest blast radius. The natural seam is `sessionUser()` in `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/online/http.ts:13-18` (it already wraps `auth()`), plus the raw `db()` calls in each route and the better-auth mount `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts:13-19`. A `try/catch` mapping the missing-DB error to e.g. 503 `{error:"online-not-configured"}` would turn the terminal 500-stack into a clean response; the client already treats non-OK as logged-out/offline (`currentUser` → null, `onlineClient`/`profilesClient` → null/false), so **no client changes are strictly required** to stop the crash — but the auth route is the one that actually fires on load and would need the same treatment. Note there is no single choke point: 17 `db()` sites + the auth mount.

**(b) `db()` falls back to `pglite://memory` in dev.** One-line-ish change at `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/db/index.ts:23-24` (e.g. default `url` to `pglite://memory` when unset and `NODE_ENV !== "production"`). Gives a *fully working* ephemeral online stack in dev with zero env (secret default already works in dev, per §4/§5). Caveats: `@electric-sql/pglite` is a **devDependency** (fine for dev, would need care to never trigger in prod), data is ephemeral per restart, and this silently changes today's "offline-first, no accounts" behavior into "accounts work but reset on restart" — which may surprise. Must keep the hard throw for `NODE_ENV=production`.

**(c) `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` flag hides online UI when no DB.** No such flag exists (§6) — you'd add one (e.g. `NEXT_PUBLIC_ONLINE_ENABLED`) and gate `AccountPanel` (sign-in/register buttons), the `onlineUsed()` probes in `GameShell.tsx:118` / `AccountPanel.tsx:29`, and the invite page. Purely cosmetic/preventive; doesn't fix an already-flagged browser unless the flag also short-circuits `currentUser()`. Cleanest "the developer never sees the 500" story, but most touch points.

**Key nuance for whichever you pick:** the bug only reproduces on a browser whose `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage flag is already set from prior online use (§2). A fresh browser is already fine today. So (b) or (a) address the *server crash*; (c) plus a check on `onlineUsed()` addresses the *stale-flag probe*. Combining (a) — so the auth route degrades cleanly — with a dev default in (b) would both silence the terminal and make local online dev zero-config.

questions.question: Removing "Play locally" from the account home cuts off the only signed-in path to local worlds — where "Upload to cloud" and "Cloud Saves / Download" live. What should happen to that feature?

options.label: Move into account menu (Recommended)
options.description: The account Singleplayer section gains an "Upload local world" action listing this browser's local worlds; picking one uploads it as a cloud singleplayer world. Feature survives, no local-menu door needed.

options.label: Drop local→cloud upload
options.description: Signed-in users create singleplayer worlds in account mode only. Existing local worlds stay local forever; the Upload/Download UI and its e2e are removed.

options.label: Keep a subtle link
options.description: No prominent button, but a small footer link (e.g. "Local worlds on this browser") still opens the local menus while signed in — upload/download stay where they are.

options.label: In-memory DB in dev (Recommended)

options.label: Strictly offline
options.description: No auto DB. API routes return a clean "online not configured" response instead of a 500 stack; account UI shows offline. Testing online features in dev still requires env setup.

options.label: Both
options.description: PGlite fallback in dev AND the clean error mapping (so a prod misconfig also degrades gracefully instead of 500ing).

Design an implementation plan for a welcome-flow rework in /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft (Next.js 16 + React 19 + TS strict + Bun voxel game; menu components in components/menu/, top-level screen machine components/GameShell.tsx; tests colocated *.test.tsx (bun test + testing-library), Playwright e2e in e2e/).

## Requirements (user-decided, final)

1. **Welcome gate**: logged-out users land on a chooser screen with exactly two actions — "Sign in" and "Play locally" (local = browser profiles, no account; copy should make clear online needs an account, local doesn't). NO "Create account" button on the gate. Shown on every launch for logged-out users; signed-in users skip it (session probe → account home). 
2. **Dedicated auth screen**: gate's "Sign in" opens a standalone auth screen (email/password sign-in form, with the existing "I need an account" toggle to flip to the create-account form). No local-profile UI on it. Needs a way back to the gate.
3. **ProfileSelect drops the embedded AccountPanel** (both branches). "Play locally" from the gate → ProfileSelect (first-run create form when no profiles, else list). ProfileSelect needs a Back-to-welcome affordance when logged out.
4. **Account home loses the prominent "Play locally" button**; replace with a SUBTLE link (small footer text link, e.g. "Local worlds on this browser") that still sets browsingLocal — Upload-to-cloud/Cloud-Saves stay in the local WorldSelect, reachable via that link. "Back to account" from local menus stays.
5. **Dev without DB**: in db/index.ts db(), when DATABASE_URL is unset and NODE_ENV !== "production", fall back to "pglite://memory" (the existing pglite branch at db/index.ts:25-40) with a one-time console notice ("DATABASE_URL not set — using in-memory PGlite; online data resets on restart. See .env.example for Postgres."). Production keeps the hard throw. Note @electric-sql/pglite is a devDependency and next.config.mjs already has serverExternalPackages for it; better-auth's default dev secret works (verified).

## Current-state facts (from exploration — trust these, file:line verified)

**GameShell.tsx**: Screen union at :29-39 (profile-select | world-select | online-worlds | play | play-cloud | play-online). State: onlineUser (:113), browsingLocal (:116), ready/screen/connecting/connectError/joiningRef. refreshOnlineUser (:117-123) gated on onlineUsed(); mount probe at :256. Resume pointer effect :234-252 sets play + browsingLocal=true (:248). Render order: play/play-cloud/play-online/world-select (:357-373, passes cloudEnabled={onlineUser!==null} :366)/online-worlds; then accountMode=onlineUser!==null (:392); accountMode&&!browsingLocal → AccountProfileSelect (:393-402, onPlayLocally→setBrowsingLocal(true) :398); fallthrough → ProfileSelect (:404-413, onAuthChange→refreshOnlineUser :410, onBackToAccount when accountMode :411).

**ProfileSelect.tsx**: props onPlay/onAuthChange?/onBackToAccount? (:10-19). firstRun branch :33-58 embeds AccountPanel at :42 + CreateProfileForm :48-55; list branch :60-145 embeds AccountPanel :63, back-to-account :64-68, new-profile :141-143.

**AccountPanel.tsx**: mode closed|signin|signup (:19). Form at :78-108 (Email/Display name/Password, submit "Create account"/"Sign in", toggle "I need an account"/"I have an account", Cancel→closed). Closed logged-out state :121-129 shows "Sign in"+"Create account" buttons (added this morning, commit 4abc9d3). markOnlineUsed in submit :57. Used by app/join/[token]/page.tsx :65 (its own signin phase — DO NOT break; keep AccountPanel's self-contained closed state working there).

**AccountProfileSelect.tsx**: props user/onPlay/onPlayLocally/onSignedOut (:22-30). Bottom row :176-189: play-locally testid button :177-179 + new-online-profile.

**WorldSelect.tsx**: cloudEnabled prop :47; Upload to cloud :97-121/:191-205; Cloud Saves section :225-239. Reached only via ProfileSelect.onPlay→world-select.

**lib/auth/client.ts**: onlineUsed/markOnlineUsed :36-44 (minecraft_online_v1), currentUser :47-52.

**db/index.ts**: db() throw at :21-24; pglite branch :25-40 (lazy require, SCHEMA_DDL from db/ddl.ts, memoized instance :19).

**Tests that WILL break and must be updated:**
- e2e/helpers.ts :46 fixture (seeds minecraft_profiles_v1 then clicks profile-e2e-profile) — used by ALL gameplay e2e; must click the gate's "Play locally" first.
- e2e/menu.e2e.ts createProfile helper :11-14 (getByLabel("Profile name") immediately) — same gate click needed.
- e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts: clicks "Sign in" (exact) → "I need an account" → ... → "Online Profiles" → getByTestId("play-locally") → ... — needs gate "Sign in" click first + play-locally becomes the subtle link.
- e2e/accountSp.e2e.ts :52-57,:104-107 and e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts signUp() :32-39 — click "Sign in" (exact) as the entry; with the gate, "Sign in" now lives on the gate → then the auth screen form. Locators may keep working if labels stay ("Sign in" gate button → form appears) — verify order.
- components/menu/ProfileSelect.test.tsx :31-32 asserts "Sign in"+"Create account" buttons on first-run (from embedded panel) — must be removed/changed.
- components/menu/AccountProfileSelect.test.tsx :83-91 play-locally door test — update to the subtle link.
- components/menu/AccountPanel.test.tsx — closed-state tests; AccountPanel itself may keep its closed state for /join (decide).

**Docs to update**: docs/online.md :25-52 (identity bullets: account-panel-on-profile-screen wording :48-52, Play-locally bullet :43-46), :68-88, :90-107; docs/manual.md :645-656 (Getting an identity), :703-715 (cloud saves flow); docs/testing.md coverage rows for changed suites; README quick start if it mentions menu flow; CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entries; docs/online.md local-dev section :155-160 + .env.example comments for the pglite dev fallback.

## Design questions to resolve in the plan

1. **New screen plumbing in GameShell**: cleanest way to add the gate + auth screen. E.g. extend the Screen union with "welcome" and "auth"? Or a separate top-level logged-out state machine? Note initial screen today is profile-select; the gate must be the logged-out root, but the resume pointer (:234-252) must still jump straight into play, and signed-in (session probe async!) users flow: ready renders... careful with flash-of-gate before the async session probe resolves for a signed-in returning user (probe only runs when onlineUsed flag set — maybe only delay-render when onlineUsed()?). Propose concrete state/flow handling the flash problem.
2. **Auth screen componentization**: reuse AccountPanel with a new prop (e.g. initialMode="signin" opening the form directly + hide closed-state) vs extract the form into a shared AccountForm used by both AccountPanel (for /join) and the new AuthScreen. Recommend one; keep /join behavior unchanged (its closed state buttons "Sign in"+"Create account" from 4abc9d3 stay).
3. **Gate component**: new components/menu/WelcomeScreen.tsx (two buttons + short copy). Which existing menu primitives to reuse (MenuScreen wrapper? mc-button classes — check components/menu/MenuScreen or similar exist: ProfileSelect uses a MenuScreen titled component per exploration).
4. **Subtle link** in AccountProfileSelect: placement/markup (footer text link, data-testid="browse-local" or keep play-locally testid to minimize e2e churn — recommend).
5. **db() dev fallback**: exact code shape (env check order, the console.warn once, keeping prod throw), plus whether .env.example/docs need a note.
6. **Commit slices** on branch improve/welcome-flow (or better name): propose 3-5 focused conventional commits, each lint-green, tests updated with the code they cover (e.g. slice 1 dev-db fallback standalone; slice 2 gate+auth screen+GameShell rewire+component tests; slice 3 account-home link + e2e updates; slice 4 docs+changelog). e2e must be green at the END (full run before PR); component tests green per slice.

## Constraints

- TS strict; no new deps; keep AGENTS.md workflow (docs+tests+CHANGELOG ship with the change; Conventional Commits, body explains why, no Co-Authored-By).
- Do not break /join/[token] or the game-server/protocol anything.
- e2e labels: prefer keeping existing accessible names ("Sign in", "Play locally"?) where sensible to minimize churn, but correctness of the new UX wins.
- The gate replaces this morning's discoverability fix (Create account button) — fine, but sign-up must remain obviously reachable via the auth screen (form toggle) and /join unchanged.

Deliver: a step-by-step implementation plan with concrete component/prop/state changes, per-file edit descriptions, the commit slicing, test-update list, and a verification section (local: format+lint+targeted bun test; full e2e run once at the end; manual dev-server pass checklist).

# Welcome-flow rework: explicit online/local gate + zero-config dev

## Context

Four user-requested UX/DX improvements: (1) the welcome page should be an explicit chooser — **Sign in** (online, needs account) vs **Play locally** (browser profiles, no account) — instead of today's local-profile screen with an embedded account panel; (2) the sign-in/create-account UI becomes a dedicated screen with no local-profile content beside it; (3) the signed-in account home drops the prominent "Play locally" button; (4) `bun run dev` must work with zero env config (currently a browser that once signed in probes `/api/auth/get-session` on load → `db()` throws `DATABASE_URL is not set` → 500 stack in the terminal).

User decisions (asked & answered): local-worlds access while signed in survives as a **subtle footer link** (Upload-to-cloud/Cloud-Saves stay in the local `WorldSelect`); dev falls back to **in-memory PGlite** (prod still hard-requires `DATABASE_URL`); the gate shows **every launch** for logged-out users (signed-in users skip it via the session probe). This supersedes part of today's `4abc9d3` (Create account button): sign-up moves off the first screen into the auth screen's existing "I need an account" toggle; `AccountPanel`'s closed state (Sign in + Create account) survives **only** on the `/join/<token>` invite page, which is untouched.

Branch: **`improve/welcome-flow`** off `main` (big work), 4 commit slices, PR at the end.

## Design

### GameShell (`components/GameShell.tsx`)

- Extend the Screen union (:29-39) with `{name:"welcome"}` (new initial state) and `{name:"auth"}`. Account home stays **derived** (`accountMode && !browsingLocal`), preserving the invariant that the async session probe can't yank an active `play*` screen.
- **Flash guard**: new `authProbed` state folded into `refreshOnlineUser` (:117-123): `onlineUsed()` false → `queueMicrotask(() => setAuthProbed(true))` (mirror the existing :241-242 lint pattern); else `currentUser().then(user => {…; setAuthProbed(true)}, () => setAuthProbed(true))` (also fixes the latent unhandled rejection). Guard **only** the welcome branch: `screen.name === "welcome" && !authProbed` → neutral `<div className="menu-screen"/>` (same as the `!ready` gate :280). Resume-to-play (:234-252) never waits on the probe.
- Root render: accountMode → `AccountProfileSelect` (its local-door handler must set **both** `setBrowsingLocal(true)` **and** `setScreen({name:"profile-select"})`; `onSignedOut` → `setOnlineUser(null)` + `setScreen({name:"welcome"})`); `screen "auth"` → `AuthScreen` (`onAuthChange={refreshOnlineUser}`, `onBack`→welcome); `screen "welcome"` → `WelcomeScreen`; fallthrough → `ProfileSelect` (drop `onAuthChange`; `onBackToAccount` when accountMode, else new `onBackToWelcome`). `world-select`/`online-worlds` `onBack` targets stay `profile-select`. After successful sign-in do NOT setScreen — the accountMode branch takes over when the probe lands.

### New/changed menu components

- **`components/menu/WelcomeScreen.tsx`** (new): `MenuScreen` + two `mc-button`s accessibly named exactly **"Sign in"** and **"Play locally"** (load-bearing for e2e), each with a `menu-note` caption *outside* the button ("Online worlds, synced profiles and cloud saves — needs a free account." / "Profiles and worlds stored in this browser — no account needed."). Testids `welcome-sign-in`/`welcome-play-locally`.
- **`components/menu/AccountForm.tsx`** (new): extract from `AccountPanel` the signin|signup form (email/name/password/busy/error, `markOnlineUsed` in submit, the "I need an account"/"I have an account" toggle). Props `{initialMode, onSuccess, onCancel?}` (Cancel button only when provided).
- **`components/menu/AuthScreen.tsx`** (new): `MenuScreen title="Sign in"` + note + `<AccountForm initialMode="signin" onSuccess={onAuthChange}/>` + `data-testid="back-to-welcome"` Back button. No closed state.
- **`components/menu/AccountPanel.tsx`**: becomes closed-state + signed-in status + `AccountForm` host. Behavior byte-identical for `/join` (keep the 4abc9d3 buttons). Accepted minor change: form fields reset on cancel (form unmounts).
- **`components/menu/ProfileSelect.tsx`**: delete both `AccountPanel` embeds (:42, :63) + the `onAuthChange` prop; add `onBackToWelcome?` rendered in **both** branches (first-run too, else a logged-out zero-profile visitor is trapped), `data-testid="back-to-welcome"`, mirroring the back-to-account pattern (:43-47/:64-68). Rewrite the first-run comment (:37-41).
- **`components/menu/AccountProfileSelect.tsx`**: remove the Play-locally button from the bottom row (:176-189, "New Profile" becomes sole primary); add footer link `<button className="menu-footer-link" data-testid="play-locally">Local worlds on this browser</button>` — **keep prop name `onPlayLocally` and testid `play-locally`** (zero cloudSaves-e2e churn). New `.menu-footer-link` class in `app/menu.css` (quiet underlined text action, opacity .7→1 on hover).

### Dev DB fallback (`db/index.ts` :21-24)

`DATABASE_URL` unset → prod: keep the throw; non-prod: `url = "pglite://memory"` + one `console.warn` ("DATABASE_URL not set — using in-memory PGlite; online data resets on restart. See .env.example for Postgres."). The `instance` memo makes the warning once-per-process; the existing pglite branch (:25-40) does the rest (`@electric-sql/pglite` devDep + `serverExternalPackages` already in place; better-auth's default dev secret verified OK). Companion: `.env.example` comment + docs/online.md "No Docker at all" (:155-160) note that bare `bun run dev` now boots the online stack ephemerally.

## Commit slices (each: format+lint+typecheck+`bun test` green)

1. **`feat(db): fall back to in-memory PGlite in dev when DATABASE_URL is unset`** — db/index.ts, new db/index.test.ts (prod-throw first, then dev-fallback + warn-once; order-aware of the memo; restore env in afterAll), .env.example, docs/online.md dev paragraph, CHANGELOG (Added).
2. **`feat(menu): welcome gate and dedicated sign-in screen`** — WelcomeScreen/AuthScreen/AccountForm (new), AccountPanel refactor, ProfileSelect, GameShell; tests: WelcomeScreen.test.tsx + AuthScreen.test.tsx (new — mock `@/lib/auth/client` mirroring the FULL export surface; bun mock.module ordering gotcha), ProfileSelect.test.tsx (drop panel asserts; assert NO sign-in controls render; back-to-welcome pair), AccountPanel.test.tsx must pass unchanged (the /join contract guard); e2e entry-path updates ride here: `e2e/helpers.ts` (after `goto("/")` click gate "Play locally" before `profile-e2e-profile`), `e2e/menu.e2e.ts` (gate click after each of the five `goto("/")`s — NOT inside `createProfile`, it's also called mid-flow), stale comments in multiplayer/cloudSaves specs.
3. **`refactor(menu): demote the account home's Play locally button to a footer link`** — AccountProfileSelect.tsx, app/menu.css, AccountProfileSelect.test.tsx (same testid still passes; assert the new accessible name).
4. **`docs(menu): document the welcome-flow rework`** — docs/online.md identity section (gate bullet; Play-locally→footer link; sign-out lands on the gate; AccountPanel now /join-only), docs/manual.md (:645-656 identity, :703-715 cloud saves), docs/testing.md rows, README quick start, CHANGELOG (Changed entry + **rescope the 4abc9d3 Fixed bullet to the invite page only** — its menu claim would ship false in the same release).

**e2e locator continuity (verified)**: cloudSaves/accountSp/multiplayer keep working without locator changes — their `getByRole("button",{name:"Sign in",exact:true})` now hits the gate, and the auth screen opens directly on the sign-in form, so the subsequent "I need an account"/labels/"Create account"/"Sign in" (submit, non-exact — unique among Back + toggle) sequences hold. cloudSaves' `getByTestId("play-locally")` hits the footer link.

## Verification

- Per slice: `bun run format` + `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, targeted `bun test components/menu` (+ `bun test db` slice 1), then full `bun test` (exit code, not `| tail`).
- End of branch: `bun run build`, full `bun run test:e2e` (gate entry paths hit all seven suites).
- Manual pass (`bun run dev`, `DATABASE_URL` unset): one-time PGlite notice; fresh storage → gate (two buttons + copy); Play locally → first-run form (no account UI, Back) → create → play → quit → Back → gate; Sign in → auth screen → Back; register → account home; footer link → local worlds (Upload to cloud → ☁ Synced) → Back to account; sign out → gate; reload signed-in → **no gate flash**; reload mid-world → resumes straight to play; `/join/<token>` logged out still shows Sign in + Create account (unchanged); dev-server restart wipes online data (matches notice).

Then push `improve/welcome-flow` and open the PR against `hutusi/monecraft` `main` (no AI-attribution lines).

lines: -# Fix co-op split-brain: two Fly machines each host their own copy of the room
+# Welcome-flow rework: explicit online/local gate + zero-config dev
## Context

-Two users joined the same online world (invite accepted, both connected cleanly), but each sees only themselves — "Players (1)", nobody else on the minimap. The application logic is provably correct: both users mint tickets for the same `wid` (`lib/online/worldsService.ts:345`, invite membership points at the owner's world id), connect to the same `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`, and within one process `RoomRegistry.getOrLoad` (`server/roomRegistry.ts:29-48`) can never create two rooms for one world (loading de-dupe, no eviction race). The e2e passes because it runs **one** server process.

+Four user-requested UX/DX improvements: (1) the welcome page should be an explicit chooser — **Sign in** (online, needs account) vs **Play locally** (browser profiles, no account) — instead of today's local-profile screen with an embedded account panel; (2) the sign-in/create-account UI becomes a dedicated screen with no local-profile content beside it; (3) the signed-in account home drops the prominent "Play locally" button; (4) `bun run dev` must work with zero env config (currently a browser that once signed in probes `/api/auth/get-session` on load → `db()` throws `DATABASE_URL is not set` → 500 stack in the terminal).

-**Root cause (verified live):** rooms exist only in per-process memory (`server/roomRegistry.ts:14`, a plain `Map`, no cross-instance coordination), and the Fly app `monecraft-server` is running **2 machines** (`fly machine list`: `rough-dust-3207` + `green-snow-5758`, both started — the default HA pair `fly launch` creates). Fly's edge load-balances each WebSocket independently, so the two players landed on different machines, each of which loaded its own copy of the world from Postgres. Nothing in `server/fly.toml` caps the count (`min_machines_running = 1` is a floor, not a ceiling; `auto_stop_machines = 'off'` keeps both alive), and `docs/deploy.md` never instructs `fly scale count 1` — the runbook gap that caused this.

+User decisions (asked & answered): local-worlds access while signed in survives as a **subtle footer link** (Upload-to-cloud/Cloud-Saves stay in the local `WorldSelect`); dev falls back to **in-memory PGlite** (prod still hard-requires `DATABASE_URL`); the gate shows **every launch** for logged-out users (signed-in users skip it via the session probe). This supersedes part of today's `4abc9d3` (Create account button): sign-up moves off the first screen into the auth screen's existing "I need an account" toggle; `AccountPanel`'s closed state (Sign in + Create account) survives **only** on the `/join/<token>` invite page, which is untouched.

-Fix = one ops command to restore prod, plus docs so it can't silently recur. No application code is wrong; adding real room affinity (fly-replay keyed on `wid`, shared room directory) is out of scope for 2–8-player co-op scale — noted as a future option only.
+Branch: **`improve/welcome-flow`** off `main` (big work), 4 commit slices, PR at the end.
-## Part 1 — Ops fix (restores prod immediately)
+## Design
-```bash
-fly scale count 1 -a monecraft-server

# Fix co-op split-brain: two Fly machines each host their own copy of the room

## Context

Two users joined the same online world (invite accepted, both connected cleanly), but each sees only themselves — "Players (1)", nobody else on the minimap. The application logic is provably correct: both users mint tickets for the same `wid` (`lib/online/worldsService.ts:345`, invite membership points at the owner's world id), connect to the same `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`, and within one process `RoomRegistry.getOrLoad` (`server/roomRegistry.ts:29-48`) can never create two rooms for one world (loading de-dupe, no eviction race). The e2e passes because it runs **one** server process.

**Root cause (verified live):** rooms exist only in per-process memory (`server/roomRegistry.ts:14`, a plain `Map`, no cross-instance coordination), and the Fly app `monecraft-server` is running **2 machines** (`fly machine list`: `rough-dust-3207` + `green-snow-5758`, both started — the default HA pair `fly launch` creates). Fly's edge load-balances each WebSocket independently, so the two players landed on different machines, each of which loaded its own copy of the world from Postgres. Nothing in `server/fly.toml` caps the count (`min_machines_running = 1` is a floor, not a ceiling; `auto_stop_machines = 'off'` keeps both alive), and `docs/deploy.md` never instructs `fly scale count 1` — the runbook gap that caused this.

Fix = one ops command to restore prod, plus docs so it can't silently recur. No application code is wrong; adding real room affinity (fly-replay keyed on `wid`, shared room directory) is out of scope for 2–8-player co-op scale — noted as a future option only.

## Part 1 — Ops fix (restores prod immediately)

```bash
fly scale count 1 -a monecraft-server
fly machine list -a monecraft-server   # expect exactly 1 started machine
```

Notes: any players connected to the destroyed machine get dropped; the client reconnect ladder mints a fresh ticket and re-syncs against the survivor (SIGTERM drain persists the dying machine's rooms — worst case a divergent copy loses the last-write race, unavoidable and minor). Verify with repeated `curl https://monecraft-server.fly.dev/health` (stable) and, with `ADMIN_TOKEN`, `GET /rooms`.

   - Step 2 (Fly deploy, lines ~76-84): add `fly scale count 1 --config server/fly.toml` after the first `fly deploy`, with the why: `fly launch` provisions a 2-machine HA pair by default, but rooms live in one process's memory — **the app must run exactly one machine** or players in the same world get split across copies.

   - Troubleshooting section: add a symptom row — "Two players in the same world can't see each other / both show Players (1)" → cause: >1 Fly machine → check `fly machine list`, fix `fly scale count 1`.
   - "Other hosts" (~lines 185-192): add "run exactly one instance" to the requirements there too.
2. **`docs/online.md`** (ops runbook, ~lines 178-206): state explicitly that rooms are in-process state and the game server must run as a **single instance** — horizontal scaling forks rooms. Reword the misleading "keeping the game server stateless" (~line 116): it's stateless only w.r.t. the web app (no web→game bridge); rooms themselves are in-memory state.
3. **`docs/architecture.md`** (~line 126): same "stateless" phrasing — add the same clarification if it reads the same way.

Full co-op on localhost: run all three, open two browser windows (one
normal, one private — each registers its own account), create an online
world in the first, and paste its invite link into the second.

**No Docker at all**: `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory` runs the web app on an
ephemeral in-process Postgres (`db/index.ts` applies the schema from
`db/ddl.ts` at boot; data lives as long as the process). Pair it with the
game server's `PERSISTENCE=memory` and the whole online stack is two
commands with zero services — exactly how the Playwright multiplayer suite
boots it (`playwright.config.ts`).

Schema lives in `db/schema.ts` (drizzle); migrations are generated with
`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs
no daemon; the auth integration test (`lib/auth/auth.test.ts`) runs the real
better-auth wiring against it, which keeps the fixture DDL, the schema
module, and the adapter honest against each other.

## Production

**[deploy.md](deploy.md) is the step-by-step first-time deploy runbook** (Neon
schema → Fly game server → Vercel web app, with a verify checklist and
troubleshooting). In short:

- **Vercel**: set the web env vars; point `DATABASE_URL` at Neon. The auth
  mount builds lazily, so `next build` needs no env.
- **Fly.io** (game server): shares `DATABASE_URL` and `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- **Online co-op — players in the same world couldn't see each other on prod** (each showed "Players (1)"): the deploy runbook now pins the Fly game server to a **single machine** (`fly scale count 1`) and documents the invariant. `fly launch` had provisioned the default two-machine HA pair; rooms live in one process's memory with no cross-instance coordination, so each machine hosted its own independent copy of the same world and the edge load-balancer split the players between them. Docs-only — no code change; the ops fix is one command on the live app.
- **Account menu — Create account is now a visible button**: the logged-out account panel (welcome/first-run screen, Local Profiles screen, and invite landing page) now shows **Create account** next to **Sign in**. Registration used to be hidden behind Sign in → "I need an account", so a new user saw no way to create an account; the in-form toggle between the two modes remains.

git add components/GameShell.tsx components/menu/WelcomeScreen.tsx components/menu/AuthScreen.tsx components/menu/AccountForm.tsx components/menu/AccountPanel.tsx components/menu/ProfileSelect.tsx components/menu/WelcomeScreen.test.tsx components/menu/AuthScreen.test.tsx components/menu/ProfileSelect.test.tsx e2e/helpers.ts e2e/menu.e2e.ts e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts && git commit -m "feat(menu): welcome gate and dedicated sign-in screen

The logged-out root mixed two identity worlds on one screen: the local
profile list (or first-run create form) with an account panel embedded
under it, which read as 'create a local profile to play' with sign-in
as an afterthought — and the panel next to a 'Create Your Profile' form
misled account holders into local profiles. The shell now roots at an
explicit welcome gate — 'Sign in' (online account) or 'Play locally'
(browser profiles, no account) — and sign-in/register lives on its own
AuthScreen with nothing local around it. Register moves off the first
screen into the form's existing 'I need an account' toggle.

The email/password form is extracted into AccountForm, shared by the
new AuthScreen and by AccountPanel, which now serves only the
/join/<token> landing page (behavior there unchanged, test-locked). A
new authProbed flag holds the neutral frame until the mount-time
session probe answers, so a signed-in reload lands on the account home
without a gate flash — and a failed probe no longer leaves an
unhandled rejection. The gate keeps the accessible names 'Sign in' /
'Play locally' with captions outside the buttons, so the existing
sign-in e2e locator sequences work unchanged; menu/gameplay specs enter
through the gate's Play locally."

## Identity: Local Players and accounts

- **Online play is accounts-only** (email/password via better-auth). There is
  no anonymous-guest layer: an invite link, cloud sync, or hosting all start
  with sign-in/register. Logged-out **Local Players** keep any number of
  browser-local profiles and worlds and make **zero** server calls.
- When signed in, the menu opens into an **account home**
  (`components/menu/AccountProfileSelect.tsx`) listing that account's
  server-side profiles (create/rename/delete, capped at `MAX_ONLINE_PROFILES`,
  synced across devices); picking one shows its worlds (`OnlineWorldSelect`)
  in two sections: **Online Worlds** (server-hosted mp rooms; the join ticket
  carries the profile's name/skin) and **Singleplayer** (`sp-cloud` worlds —
  full client-side engine, **no game server**, saves synced to the account so
  any signed-in device continues them). Owned worlds of both kinds share the
  `MAX_WORLDS_PER_PROFILE` cap. Worlds joined by invite are account-level
  memberships, so they appear under **every** profile with a "Joined" tag;
  so do singleplayer saves uploaded from the local menus (`profileId` null —
  account-level).
- Local worlds are **hidden but preserved** while signed in — never deleted,
  never auto-uploaded. The account home's **"Play locally"** button opens the
  local menus without signing out (that's also where cloud-save sync lives);
  "Back to account" returns. Signing out lands on the local flow directly.
- Sessions are better-auth cookies; the game server never sees them.
- The Account panel renders on the profile-select screen **and on the
  first-run create-profile screen** (`components/menu/ProfileSelect.tsx`), so
  sign in / register is reachable before any local profile exists. Logged out
  it offers **Sign in** and **Create account** side by side (the form also has
  an in-form toggle between the two modes).

## Worlds, invites, cloud saves

640	contents of every chest — so the world regenerates identically and picks up where
641	you left off. Because saves
642	live in the browser, they're tied to that browser on that device; "Reset" starts a
643	fresh world.
644	
645	## Playing online
646	
647	Online worlds are shared worlds that live on a server and hold **2–8 players** —
648	private co-op with people you invite, not public matchmaking. Everything offline
649	stays exactly as it is: local worlds never need an account or a connection.
650	
651	**Getting an identity.** Online play needs an **account** — a one-time
652	email/password registration from the **Account** panel on the profile screen
653	(or right on an invite page). Signed in, the menu becomes your account home:
654	up to five **online profiles** (name + skin) that follow you across devices,
655	each owning its online worlds. Your local worlds stay put — press **Play
656	locally** to visit them (and their cloud-save controls) without signing out.
657	
658	**Hosting.** Pick an online profile to see its worlds. **New Online World**
659	uses the same form as a local world (name, seed, world type, mode,

## Playing online

Online worlds are shared worlds that live on a server and hold **2–8 players** —
private co-op with people you invite, not public matchmaking. Everything offline
stays exactly as it is: local worlds never need an account or a connection.

**Getting an identity.** Online play needs an **account** — a one-time
email/password registration from the **Account** panel on the profile screen
(or right on an invite page). Signed in, the menu becomes your account home:
up to five **online profiles** (name + skin) that follow you across devices,
each owning its online worlds. Your local worlds stay put — press **Play
locally** to visit them (and their cloud-save controls) without signing out.

**Hosting.** Pick an online profile to see its worlds. **New Online World**
uses the same form as a local world (name, seed, world type, mode,
difficulty); creating it connects you straight in. Press **Copy invite** on
your world's card to put a join link on the clipboard — send it to your
friends. Invite links expire after a while; copy a fresh one any time.

**Singleplayer, synced.** A profile can also hold **singleplayer** worlds
(**New Singleplayer World** on the same screen): they play exactly like local
worlds — entirely on your machine, no game-server connection — but the save
lives with your account, so signing in on another computer picks up right
where you left off. Online and singleplayer worlds share the same per-profile
limit.

**Joining.** Opening an invite link shows the world's name and asks you to
sign in (or register) if you aren't; the world then joins your account and
shows up in every profile's world list with a **Joined** tag — click its card
to play. The world is yours to rejoin from that list from then on; the link
is only needed once.

**Playing together.** Everyone shares one world: block edits, mobs, chests,
day and night. You'll see the other players in the world with their names
overhead, and a player list in the top-right corner. Press **`T`** (or
`Enter`) to chat; a ping badge shows your connection quality, and losing the
connection pops a notice with the option to leave. The **server** owns the
world — your mining completes when it confirms the break (a barely-noticeable
beat on a good connection), and your health, hunger, and inventory are its
word, not the client's.

A few things work differently online, and the rest is the same game:

- **Pause is personal.** `Esc` opens your menu but the world keeps running —
  nobody can stop a shared world. "Save & Quit" becomes **Leave world**.
- **Sleeping needs everyone.** The night skips only when **all** players are
  in bed (dead and Spectator players excepted) — climb back out to cancel.
- **Progress is your own.** Advancements, statistics, XP, and kill credit are
  per-player — you earn your own, whether the kill was a sword, an arrow, or
  your pet's doing. Your pet follows **you**, not the nearest player.
- **The world owner can kick.** If you created the world, the player list shows
  a **Kick** button beside everyone else (free your cursor with `Esc` to click
  it) — for removing a griefer on the spot. To stop them coming back, also
  **Revoke links** from the world's menu card.
- **Boats are shared.** Rafts and ships are boardable online — pile into one
  together.
- The world saves on the server automatically; there's nothing to manage.

### Cloud saves — your single-player worlds across devices

Signed in, you can make a **single-player** world follow you between browsers
and machines. On the world's card, **Upload to cloud** copies it to your
account (the card then reads **☁ Synced**), and from there every save syncs up
automatically as you play. On another device, your synced worlds appear under
**Cloud Saves** — **Download** brings one onto that device to play.

It's last-write-wins: if the same world is played on two devices, the most
recent save wins. Open a synced world and it always catches up to the latest
first; a world you played offline keeps its newer progress rather than being
overwritten by an older cloud copy. Local worlds you never upload stay entirely
offline, exactly as before — cloud saves are opt-in, one world at a time.

## Worlds & profiles

The game opens to a menu rather than dropping you straight into a world:

1. **Choose how to play.** The game opens with two doors: **Sign in** (online
   worlds and cloud saves — needs a free account, see
   [Playing online](#playing-online)) or **Play locally** (everything below —
   stored in this browser, no account).
2. **Pick a profile.** A profile is a player — a name and an appearance (skin). On a
   shared browser everyone can have their own. Create one with **New Profile**, choose
   a skin, and you're in; rename or delete profiles from the same screen.
2. **Pick a world.** Each profile keeps its **own** list of worlds. **New World** lets
   you name it, choose a **world type** (Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands —
   see [the reference](reference.md#world-types)), and optionally enter a **seed** —
   type a number or a word to get the same world every time, or leave it blank for a
   random one. Worlds you've played show most-recent first; rename or delete them here too.
3. **Play.** Choosing a world drops you in. From the pause menu (**Esc**), **Save &
   Quit to Worlds** takes you back to the list, and reloading the page resumes the
   world you were in.

Everything is saved in your browser (localStorage). Deleting a world removes its save;
deleting a profile removes all of its worlds.

# Monecraft (Next.js + TypeScript + Three.js + Bun)

[![CI](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/hutusi/monecraft?label=release&sort=semver)](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/tags)

A playable, Minecraft-inspired voxel game that runs entirely in your browser. Explore procedural terrain across five biomes, cross water by **raft** or **ship** — over living oceans with **fish**, **kelp**, sunken **shipwrecks** to dive, and **buried treasure** to hunt by map — and dig into **dark caves** — lit only by the torches you craft and place, where lava pools and mobs lurk. Mine ores, raid **underground dungeons** for loot, build and farm, breed animals, craft through seven gear tiers up to a **bow** and throwable **spears**, and take on an **endgame boss** for a true win condition — all across a day-night cycle with hunger, drowning, and lava hazards.

The twist: **everything is procedural — zero binary assets.** Block textures and item sprites are painted from pixel code, all sound and music is synthesized at runtime, and lighting is computed per voxel. Single-player is client-only: keep **multiple worlds** under **multiple player profiles**, all saved to localStorage, no account needed. Or play **online co-op** (2–8 players): host a server-backed world with a free account and share an invite link — friends register and join in a click. See [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md#playing-online).

## Run

```bash
bun install
bun run dev
```

Then open `http://localhost:3000`.

The game opens to a menu: pick or create a **profile** (your name and look), then create or choose a **world** to play. New worlds let you pick a **type** — Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands — a **game mode**, a **difficulty** (Peaceful · Easy · Normal · Hard), an optional **Hardcore** toggle (permadeath, locked to Survival + Hard), and a seed. Each profile keeps its own list of worlds, so several players can share one browser. Inside the game, **Esc → Save & Quit to Worlds** returns to the world list.

## Controls

- `W A S D`: Move · `Space`: Jump · `C`: Crouch
- `W + CapsLock`: Sprint (drains hunger)
- Double-tap `Space`: Toggle flight in Creative (Spectator always flies); then `Space` / `C` to rise / descend
- `Mouse`: Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)
- `Left click` (hold): Break block / attack mobs
- `Right click` or `E`: Place/interact, board rafts, place water vehicles, or throw a selected spear
- `1..9`: Select hotbar slot
- `I`: Inventory & crafting · `L`: Advancements & statistics · `F`: Eat food · `Shift+U`: Emergency unstuck
- `V`: Camera view (first-person → third-person rear → third-person front)
- `T` or `Enter`: Chat (online worlds)
- `Esc`: Pause menu — three tabs: **Game** (save / load / reset, **Save & Quit to Worlds**, the **Game Mode** and **Difficulty** switchers), **Options** (sound/music volume, Appearance skins), and **Controls** · `F3`: Debug overlay

New here? The [player manual](docs/manual.md) walks through your first day, survival, crafting, farming, mobs, and more.

## Development

```bash
bun run lint        # ESLint
bun run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
bun test            # unit + integration + component tests
bun run build       # production build
bun run test:e2e    # Playwright browser smoke tests
bun run format      # Prettier
```

All of these are enforced by CI on every PR. The game simulation is a headless engine (no DOM), so gameplay logic is covered by real simulation tests, and a Playwright smoke suite exercises the browser layers — see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md).

## Docs

- [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md) — player guide: getting started, survival, crafting, mobs, farming
- [docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md) — scannable tables: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item stats
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) — engine/renderer/shell layering and invariants
- [docs/adding-content.md](docs/adding-content.md) — add a block, item, recipe, mob, or mechanic
- [docs/save-format.md](docs/save-format.md) — save schema and compatibility rules
- [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md) — deploy online multiplayer (Vercel + Neon + Fly.io)
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — workflow and verification baseline

1	import { defineConfig, devices } from "@playwright/test";
2	
3	/**
4	 * E2E smoke tests run against the production build (next start) — the dev
5	 * server's React StrictMode double-mounts the game engine and would make
6	 * runs slower and noisier.
7	 *
8	 * Files are named *.e2e.ts (NOT *.test.ts / *.spec.ts) so `bun test` does not
9	 * try to execute them with its own runner.
10	 */
11	export default defineConfig({
12	  testDir: "e2e",
13	  testMatch: "**/*.e2e.ts",
14	  fullyParallel: false,
15	  forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,
16	  retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,
17	  workers: 1,
18	  reporter: process.env.CI ? [["github"], ["html", { open: "never" }]] : "list",
19	  timeout: 60000,
20	  use: {
21	    baseURL: "http://localhost:3000",
22	    trace: "retain-on-failure"
23	  },
24	  // channel "chromium" runs the full browser in new-headless mode: the default
25	  // headless shell rejects requestPointerLock (WrongDocumentError).
26	  projects: [{ name: "chromium", use: { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"], channel: "chromium" } }],
27	  webServer: [
28	    {
29	      // The web app with a full online stack and ZERO external services: an
30	      // ephemeral in-process Postgres (pglite://) backs accounts/worlds, and
31	      // the game server below is where its join tickets point.
32	      command: "bun run build && bun run start",
33	      url: "http://localhost:3000",
34	      reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
35	      timeout: 180000,
36	      env: {
37	        DATABASE_URL: "pglite://memory",
38	        BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: "e2e-secret-e2e-secret-e2e-secret",
39	        BETTER_AUTH_URL: "http://localhost:3000",
40	        GAME_TICKET_SECRET: "e2e-ticket-secret",
41	        NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL: "ws://localhost:18080"
42	      }
43	    },
44	    {
45	      // The game server, database-free (rooms persist in memory for the run).
46	      command: "bun server/index.ts",
47	      url: "http://localhost:18080/health",
48	      reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
49	      timeout: 60000,
50	      env: {
51	        PORT: "18080",
52	        PERSISTENCE: "memory",
53	        GAME_TICKET_SECRET: "e2e-ticket-secret"
54	      }
55	    }
56	  ]
57	});

gh pr create --repo hutusi/monecraft --base main --head improve/welcome-flow --title "Welcome-flow rework: explicit online/local gate + zero-config dev" --body "## What

Four UX/DX improvements to how the game opens, as one reviewable unit (4 commits):

1. **Welcome gate** (\`feat(menu)\`): logged out, the first screen is now an explicit choice — **Sign in** or **Play locally** — instead of the local-profile screen with an account panel embedded under it. Sign-in/register moves to a dedicated **AuthScreen** (register via the form's \"I need an account\" toggle); \`ProfileSelect\` is purely local again and gains a Back to the gate. A signed-in reload skips the gate with **no flash** (the shell holds a neutral frame until the session probe answers — which also fixes a latent unhandled rejection on a failed probe). Sign-out lands on the gate.
2. **Account home** (\`refactor(menu)\`): the prominent **Play locally** button becomes a quiet **\"Local worlds on this browser\"** footer link — signed-in play reads as the online profiles, while local worlds (and their cloud-save Upload/Download) stay one click away. Same testid/callback, so the cloud-saves e2e needed zero locator changes.
3. **Zero-config dev** (\`feat(db)\`): \`bun run dev\` with no \`DATABASE_URL\` now falls back to an ephemeral in-memory PGlite (one-time console notice) instead of 500-ing on the first online request. Production keeps the hard error. The URL decision is extracted into \`resolveDatabaseUrl()\` and unit-tested.
4. **Docs** (\`docs(menu)\`): online.md identity section, manual.md (incl. the getting-started list), testing.md coverage rows, README, deploy.md verify step, CHANGELOG — plus rescoping the earlier \"Create account button\" bullet to the invite page, which this gate supersedes in the main menu.

The shared email/password form is extracted into \`AccountForm\`; \`AccountPanel\` (closed state with Sign in + Create account) now serves only the \`/join/<token>\` invite page, byte-identically — its tests pass unchanged as the contract guard.

## Verification

- \`bun test\`: **1145 pass, exit 0** (incl. new WelcomeScreen/AuthScreen/resolveDatabaseUrl suites); lint / typecheck / format:check / \`bun run build\` green.
- **Playwright e2e: 22/22 passed** — the gate keeps the accessible names \"Sign in\" / \"Play locally\", so the three sign-in journeys (multiplayer, cloudSaves, accountSp) run with **no locator changes**; menu/gameplay specs enter through the gate's Play locally.
- Manual dev pass with **no env at all**: server prints the one-time PGlite notice, \`/api/auth/get-session\` returns a clean \`null\` (previously a 500 stack), and a real registration round-trips against the ephemeral DB.

## Notes for review

- The gate shows on every logged-out launch (deliberate — signed-in sessions skip it automatically).
- Local worlds while signed in remain reachable only via the footer link; the resume-a-tab flow and \`/join\` invite flow are untouched." 2>&1 | tail -2

All four improvements are implemented, fully verified, and up for review as **PR #51**: https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/pull/51 (branch `improve/welcome-flow`, 4 commits).

**What you'll see now:**
1. **Welcome gate** — logged out, the game opens on exactly two buttons: **Sign in** and **Play locally**, each with a one-line caption (account needed vs. browser-only). No "Create account" up front; registration lives inside the sign-in screen's "I need an account" toggle.
2. **Dedicated sign-in screen** — no local-profile form anywhere near it, with a Back to the gate. The old account panel now exists only on the `/join/<token>` invite page, unchanged.
3. **Account home without "Play locally"** — signed in, you see your online profiles only; the local worlds (and their cloud-save Upload/Download) survive behind a quiet underlined footer link, "Local worlds on this browser," per your choice.
4. **Zero-config dev** — `bun run dev` with no env now prints a one-time notice and runs on an in-memory PGlite: I verified the session probe that used to 500 returns a clean `null`, and a real account registration round-trips. Data resets on restart; production still hard-requires `DATABASE_URL`.

**Verification:** 1145 unit/component tests (exit 0), lint/typecheck/format/build green, and **22/22 Playwright e2e** — the gate keeps the exact button names the sign-in journeys click, so the three account e2e specs passed without locator changes.

One thing worth knowing: the first e2e run appeared to fail completely — every test timed out. The cause was environmental: **another project's dev server ("Amytis") is occupying port 3000 on your machine**, and Playwright's `reuseExistingServer` pointed every test at that app instead of Monecraft. I re-ran the suite on port 3100 via a throwaway config (deleted after) rather than kill your process. If you run `bun run test:e2e` yourself, stop that server first or it will do the same thing.

Also noted in the PR: a signed-in reload skips the gate with no flash (the shell waits for the session probe behind a neutral frame), and mid-tab world resume is untouched.

file.content:
# Bun is pinned (not "latest") for reproducibility. Since worldgen v11 the pin
# is no longer load-bearing for the worldgen hash tests — seed-determined noise
# is bit-portable across JS engines (lib/world/noise.ts, proven by
# e2e/determinism.e2e.ts) — so a Bun bump should NOT shift those digests; if it
# ever does, that's a portability bug, not a re-baseline. See docs/testing.md.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run lint
      - run: bun run typecheck
      - run: bun run format:check
      - run: bun test
      - run: bun run build
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"

  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: bun run test:e2e
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 7

content.content:
84:The digests are also an **engine-portability contract**: since worldgen v11, every seed-determined noise call uses the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts` (polynomial sine, integer hashes — only IEEE-exact operations), so the same seed generates identical bytes on every JS engine. `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves it in CI by recomputing the full-size world digest inside Chromium/V8 and asserting it equals the Bun/JSC baseline in `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` — this is what lets a browser client and a multiplayer Bun server share worlds by seed + block diff. `lib/world/noise.test.ts` additionally pins exact golden doubles of the noise primitives. New worldgen code must import its noise/trig from `lib/world/noise.ts`, never `Math.sin`/`Math.cos` (engine-defined per ECMA-262 — the reason the old digests were only valid on a pinned Bun).
86:The **portable-noise worldgen (v10 → v11)** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline: same wave formulas on `portableSin`/`portableCos`, plus an integer-hash `hash2D`. All seven digests re-rolled; **every structural probe passed unchanged** — the polynomial sine tracks the real one within ~6e-8, so terrain structure is preserved and only scattered single-block flips (cobble speckle, cave edges, flora patterns) moved the hashes. This bump also retired the old "case 2" (a Bun version bump could shift `Math.sin` results): the CI Bun pin is no longer load-bearing for worldgen, though it stays pinned for plain reproducibility.

+- **Game server rightsized to its real usage**: the Fly VM drops from 2 GB to **512 MB** (still `shared-cpu-2x`), and with it `MAX_ROOMS` from 6 to **3** — rooms are ~74 MB each, so the two must scale together or a full house would OOM the machine. PRs keep the full verify gate (lint, typecheck, format, tests, build); e2e still gates what actually lands on `main`, and renderer/input/shell changes run it locally before landing per AGENTS.md.

- **The menu now opens on a welcome gate**: logged out, the first screen is an explicit choice — **Sign in** (online worlds, synced profiles, cloud saves; opens a dedicated sign-in screen whose "I need an account" toggle registers) or **Play locally** (browser profiles and worlds, no account) — replacing the local-profile screen with an account panel embedded under it, which read as "create a local profile to play" and misled new users about where accounts fit. Sign-in/register is a standalone screen with no local-profile UI beside it; the local menus gain a Back to the gate; signing out lands on the gate. A signed-in reload skips the gate entirely (no flash) straight to the account home, and resuming a world mid-tab is untouched. On the account home, the prominent **Play locally** button becomes a quiet **"Local worlds on this browser"** footer link — signed-in play lives in the online profiles, while local worlds (and their cloud-save Upload/Download) stay one click away.

**Welcome-flow rework (2026-07-05): PR #51 OPEN** (https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/pull/51, branch `improve/welcome-flow`, 4 commits `76cf24e/5070177/068324d/af33c58`), awaiting user review. Full gate green: 1145 bun tests exit 0, 22/22 e2e, build, lint, typecheck, format. Supersedes the menu half of the "Create account button" fix (`4abc9d3`, now `/join`-only — CHANGELOG rescoped).

User-decided design (asked via AskUserQuestion): local-worlds access while signed in = **quiet footer link** "Local worlds on this browser" (keeps testid `play-locally`); dev DB = **in-memory PGlite fallback** when `DATABASE_URL` unset outside production (`resolveDatabaseUrl()` in `db/index.ts`); gate shows **every logged-out launch** (signed-in reload skips via `authProbed` neutral-frame guard in GameShell).

Key structure: `WelcomeScreen` (two buttons, captions OUTSIDE buttons — accessible names "Sign in"/"Play locally" are load-bearing for e2e locators), `AuthScreen` (dedicated, opens in signin mode), `AccountForm` (extracted from `AccountPanel`; the panel now serves only `/join/<token>`). GameShell Screen union gained `welcome` (initial) + `auth`; account home stays derived (`accountMode && !browsingLocal`); the local-door handler must set BOTH `browsingLocal` AND `screen` or it bounces to the gate.

Gotchas learned:
- **Constructing PGlite under happy-dom breaks** (its URL polyfill vs the CJS bundle's `new URL`) — that's why `resolveDatabaseUrl` is tested instead of `db()`; the pglite branch itself is proven by e2e.
- **Port 3000 occupied by another project's dev server ("Amytis", node) on this machine** — Playwright's `reuseExistingServer: !CI` latched onto it and ALL 22 e2e failed with timeouts waiting for buttons (page snapshot showed the wrong app). Fix: one-off untracked config on port 3100 (deleted after). If e2e inexplicably all-fail locally, check `lsof -iTCP:3000` FIRST.
- Next typegen marks `process.env.NODE_ENV` readonly — tests mutate via `process.env as Record<string, string | undefined>`.

content.text:
Both done, as two local commits on `improve/welcome-flow` (not pushed):

**1. Fly VM rightsizing (`c09dd44`)** — worth doing, with one coupling I handled: the 2 GB wasn't sized for observed load but for capacity — `MAX_ROOMS = 6` × ~74 MB/room ≈ 444 MB of rooms plus the Bun runtime. Dropping memory to 512 MB while leaving `MAX_ROOMS = 6` would OOM the machine if six worlds ever loaded at once. So `server/fly.toml` now has **512 MB (still `shared-cpu-2x`) with `MAX_ROOMS = 3`**, a comment saying the two scale together, and deploy.md updated (6 rooms needs ~1 GB). Two things to know:
- The repo change only takes effect on the next `bun run deploy:server` — or resize the live machine now with `fly scale memory 512 -a monecraft-server`.
- The visible trade-off is capacity: at most 3 concurrent online worlds ticking (a 4th join is refused at the door). At current player counts that's plenty, and raising it later is one scale command plus the env.

**2. e2e off PRs (`593813b`)** — agreed, and it's the standard shape for a solo fork: the `e2e` job now has `if: github.event_name == 'push'`, so it runs only when something lands on `main` (your CI triggers are exactly `push: main` + `pull_request`). PRs still run the full verify job (lint, typecheck, format, tests, build), and AGENTS.md already requires a local e2e run for renderer/input/shell changes before landing. The one real trade-off: an e2e-only breakage now surfaces *after* merge instead of before — acceptable given you'd see it on the merge commit immediately and e2e-relevant changes get local runs anyway.

Both have CHANGELOG entries, and format/lint are green. One cosmetic note: both changelog bullets rode in the server commit rather than split across the two. When you're happy, `git push` will add them to PR #51 — the PR description doesn't mention these two yet, so I can append a note to it after you push if you'd like.
